content.content: Only an operation that names the change it acted on and kept work is recorded. A bracket records a creation, a recording or a removal when the run answers the target — the born change, the recorded-into node, the removed change — and its window kept at least one entry; it records nothing when it answers none or kept none: no marker is appended, so no marker names an empty target and no no-op buys an un-undoable step.
content.rationale: S5-bracket (otmxqplr) fixes the read-run-read protocol and the window it keeps; this fixes which of those brackets become a record. A marker is one operation's own record — its kind, the change it targeted, its kept entry ids and its reverts (G-marker, kkqzyxly) — and with no change there is nothing for the record to hold. Undo takes each kind's inverse, and a creation's is removing the change it targeted (D8a, prsoxsuo), so a marker with no target is a step undo cannot cross and the stack would refuse at it. S5-lifecycle (vwlrqoxk) fixes which invocations bracket, and S5-birth-fail (kvwonkzy) the case that motivates the rule: a refused birth has already abandoned the change it opened, so nothing remains for a record to point at. Recording the empty target instead would buy an un-undoable step and a schema exception; naming the change or recording nothing keeps the record and the inverse aligned. A run that kept no entries moved nothing, so a marker for it would be the same un-undoable step: undo could only cross it by doing nothing. The recording that motivates the rule is `deccy record --to` naming the change the working copy is already on — the placement is a no-op and the edit is already the target's, so there is nothing for a marker to hold and the history stays equal to the work that landed.
